description: Sends each clock tick at random to an A side or a B side and holds a fresh random voltage for whichever side was picked

params.text: Sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16, each drawing its own random numbers
Sets the balance between the two sides, every tick going to A fully clockwise, every tick going to B fully counter-clockwise, and an even split at noon, the other way round from the maker's tooltip
Sets the span of the random voltages, 0 to 10V
Adds an offset of -5V to 5V to every random voltage, setting the bottom of the random range rather than its middle, despite the maker's Center label
In latch a side's gate stays high until the other side is picked and its voltage holds until then; in passthrough the clock passes through and a new voltage is drawn every tick

inputs.text: A rising edge picks a side for each channel and draws new random voltages
Shifts the balance between the two sides, 5V sending every tick to A and -5V sending every tick to B

outputs.text: Carries a gate on each channel whose most recent tick went to A, 10V in latch and the incoming clock voltage in passthrough
The random voltage held for the A side, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs
Carries a gate on each channel whose most recent tick went to B, 10V in latch and the incoming clock voltage in passthrough
The random voltage held for the B side, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs
An echo of the incoming clock on every channel
A new random voltage drawn on every tick whichever side was picked, scaled and offset by the Rand CV knobs

notes: nothing is drawn and nothing moves until a rising edge arrives at the clock input.
a polyphonic clock is summed to one signal before the edge is read, so every channel takes its pick from the same edge.
